q6_regime_labels_and_spy_refreshes.spy_csv_is: a close series only - date,close, 2424 rows
q6_regime_labels_and_spy_refreshes.measured_by: regime.py has zero persistence calls; load_spy_regime runs the HMM decode per read
q6_regime_labels_and_spy_refreshes.therefore: both refresh times are sufficient BY CONSTRUCTION - there is no materialisation step that could lag behind a SPY update
q6_regime_labels_and_spy_refreshes.1345_refresh: runs before the close and can never carry today's bar; the gate does not ask for it - required_daily_close_through is the last trading day BEFORE today, the same answer all day
q6_regime_labels_and_spy_refreshes.1620_refresh: writes today's close, which is exactly what the next morning needs
q6_regime_labels_and_spy_refreshes.verified_by: RegimeLabels.get uses asof(day - lag); Monday lag 1 asks Sunday, gets Friday
q6_regime_labels_and_spy_refreshes.holidays: required_daily_close_through uses prev_trading_day, the same trading calendar

caveat.what: verify_regime_labels ONLY warns - every path returns 0
paths: labels actually changed -> warn, return count
caveat.consequence_1: a label drift does not fail the job; update_spy_csv succeeds, the journal shows success, the dashboard shows nothing
caveat.consequence_2: 'verified, no drift' and 'could not verify' both return 0 - the tri-state defect this route removed from its broker reads, still standing here
caveat.recommendation: make it a child failure, visible as the same job's failure, before the first paper order
caveat.why_not: a behaviour change to a shared job; this stage's remit was reader-level
